Keywords: One Health, Pandemic preparedness, Turkish healthcare system, Zoonotic diseases Received: June 11, 2026 Accepted: October 16, 2026 1. Introduction Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to challenge global health security, demonstrating the need for sustained preparedness beyond individual epidemic events. Outbreaks of severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), together with renewed concerns about avian influenza A(H5N1) and hantavirus infections, illustrate the diverse and evolving nature of infectious disease threats. The risk of future outbreaks is shaped by interconnected factors, including environmental change, biodiversity loss, urbanization, international travel, and increased interactions between humans, animals, and their shared environments. Consequently, pandemic preparedness requires more than adequate clinical capacity; it Int. J. of Health Serv. Res. and Policy (2026) 11(3):270-280 https://doi.org/10.33457/ijhsrp.1969304 271 also depends on effective surveillance, timely risk assessment, intersectoral coordination, and international cooperation. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed substantial differences in countries’ capacities to prevent, detect, and respond to public health emergencies, reinforcing the importance of strengthening preparedness at both national and global levels. The adoption of the World Health Organization’s Pandemic Agreement in 2025 further underscored international efforts to improve pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response [1]. The emergence of zoonotic diseases is closely associated with ecological and environmental changes that alter interactions among humans, wildlife, and domestic animals. Evidence indicates that zoonotic host diversity can increase in human-dominated ecosystems, while climate change may alter opportunities for viral transmission between species [2], [3]. These findings reinforce the importance of understanding infectious disease emergence through an integrated perspective rather than considering human health in isolation. The One Health approach provides a framework for addressing the interconnectedness of human, animal, and environmental health and has been increasingly emphasized in research on emerging infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness [4], [5]. Against this background, this study examines major infectious disease outbreaks with global public health implications, considers factors that may contribute to future pandemic risks, and assesses Türkiye’s preparedness for potential future outbreaks using a SWOT analysis framework. 2. Materials and Methods 2.1. Research Type This study employed a descriptive review design based on a structured literature search and document analysis. The review examined scientific publications and official institutional documents concerning major infectious disease outbreaks, zoonotic risks, and pandemic preparedness, with particular emphasis on Türkiye’s healthcare system. The review was not designed as a systematic review; rather, it aimed to synthesize relevant documentary evidence and interpret the findings using a SWOT framework. The analysis focused on identifying reported healthcare capacities, structural challenges, opportunities for improvement, and potential threats to Türkiye’s preparedness for future global outbreaks. 2.2. Data Sources This study was based exclusively on secondary sources and did not involve primary data collection or direct interaction with human participants. The sources included scientific publications and official reports from the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health, the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), and the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), as well as other relevant institutional documents and peer-reviewed publications. 2.3. Literature Search Strategy and Eligibility Criteria The review included scientific publications and official institutional documents addressing major infectious disease outbreaks, zoonotic risks, and pandemic preparedness, with particular emphasis on Türkiye’s healthcare system. Eligible sources were required to provide relevant information on disease emergence, outbreak management, surveillance, healthcare system capacity, or pandemic preparedness. Peer-reviewed articles, official reports, and relevant institutional documents were considered for inclusion. Duplicate records, sources with insufficient methodological information, and publications unrelated to the study objectives were excluded. The review focused on seven disease groups identified in the study title: SARS, influenza A(H1N1), Ebola virus disease, COVID-19, mpox, avian influenza A(H5N1), and hantavirus infections. Int. J. of Health Serv. Res. and Policy (2026) 11(3):270-280 https://doi.org/10.33457/ijhsrp.1969304 272 2.4. Document Review Procedure Data were collected through the examination of scientific publications and official institutional documents. The reviewed sources were assessed for information concerning disease characteristics, outbreak management, surveillance systems, healthcare infrastructure, and national and international pandemic preparedness. Relevant information was recorded and organized according to its relevance to the study objectives and the SWOT framework. No primary data collection instrument was used because the study relied exclusively on secondary sources. 2.5. Literature Search and Selection Process The literature search covered publications from 2002 to 2026. Sources were identified through searches of publications and reports issued by the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health, the YÖK National Thesis Center, TR Index (ULAKBİM), the TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM Medical Database, DergiPark, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Türk Medline, and Google Scholar. Search terms included “pandemic preparedness,” “zoonotic diseases,” “One Health,” “Turkish healthcare system,” “SARS,” “H1N1,” “Ebola,” “COVID-19,” “Mpox,” “H5N1,” and “Hantavirus.” These terms were used individually and in combination, where appropriate. Records were assessed for relevance to the study objectives, publication type, and contribution to the understanding of pandemic preparedness and zoonotic disease risks. Duplicate records, publications with insufficient methodological information, and sources unrelated to the research objectives were excluded. 2.6. Data Analysis The included documents were analyzed qualitatively using a descriptive approach. Relevant information concerning Türkiye’s preparedness for emerging infectious diseases and future pandemics was identified and organized according to the study objectives. The extracted information was classified into four SWOT categories: strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Strengths and weaknesses represented reported internal capacities and challenges of the healthcare and preparedness systems, whereas opportunities and threats represented external developments and conditions that could influence preparedness. The resulting categories were interpreted in relation to the documentary evidence reviewed. This approach provided the analytical basis for the SWOT findings presented in the Results section. 3. Results 3.1. SWOT Analysis for Türkiye 3.1.1 Strengths • Strengthened public health infrastructure and outbreak management experience following COVID-19 • Advanced laboratory capacity and widespread molecular diagnostic methods • Digital surveillance and infectious disease monitoring systems operated by the Ministry of Health • Experience gained in filiation and contact tracing practices • Extensive hospital network and high intensive care capacity • Increasing academic interest in the One Health approach • Improved emergency management capacity after COVID-19 • Strengthened vaccine and pharmaceutical logistics infrastructure Int. J. of Health Serv. Res. and Policy (2026) 11(3):270-280 https://doi.org/10.33457/ijhsrp.1969304 273 3.1.2 Weaknesses • Insufficient zoonotic disease surveillance systems • Deficiencies in rodent population control • Limited public awareness regarding zoonotic infections • Biosafety challenges in rural areas • Limited implementation of the One Health approach • Healthcare workforce shortages and burnout risks • Inadequate virus-specific national preparedness and emergency response plans 3.1.3 Opportunities • Increased healthcare investments after COVID-19 • Expanding collaborations with WHO and international organizations • Development of artificial intelligence–supported epidemiological surveillance systems • Increasing cooperation between universities and the Ministry of Health • Potential for developing digital early warning systems • Advancements in domestic vaccine and biotechnology production capacity • Integration potential of the One Health approach into national health policies • Increasing academic research on zoonotic diseases • Expansion of community-based public health education programs • Opportunities for integration among veterinary medicine, environmental health, and human health sectors 3.1.4 Threats • Increasing rodent populations associated with climate change • Emergence of new zoonotic diseases • Increased transmission risks associated with global travel and trade • Environmental hygiene problems in rural areas • Increased rodent exposure risks in agricultural settings • Delayed diagnosis and intervention in rare infectious diseases • Potential burden of global outbreaks on the healthcare system • Biological risks associated with international food trade and logistics • Misinformation and infodemic-related risks 4. Historical Development of Pandemic and Increasing Global Risk 4.1. SARS (2002-2003) Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) emerged in southern China in 2002 and spread internationally, demonstrating how rapidly an emerging infectious disease can cross national borders through international travel. The outbreak highlighted the importance of early case detection, infection prevention and control, contact tracing, and coordinated international surveillance. The outbreak was brought under control in 2003 following coordinated international surveillance and public health interventions, highlighting the importance of early detection, case identification, and infection control in containing emerging infectious diseases [6]. 4.2. Influenza A/H1N1 (Swine Flu) Pandemic (2009) Influenza A/H1N1 was a global influenza pandemic that emerged in 2009. Commonly referred to as “swine flu” because it was initially identified in pigs, the disease rapidly evolved into a global Int. J. of Health Serv. Res. and Policy (2026) 11(3):270-280 https://doi.org/10.33457/ijhsrp.1969304 274 pandemic due to its high transmissibility, despite having a lower mortality rate compared with SARS. Particularly high infection rates among young adults attracted considerable attention. Following the H1N1 pandemic, many countries updated their pandemic preparedness plans, strengthened influenza surveillance systems, and increased vaccine production capacity [7]. Today, H1N1 remains among the circulating seasonal influenza strains and continues to be monitored as an important global public health concern. WHO officially declared the H1N1 outbreak a pandemic in 2009 [7]. 4.3. Ebola Virus Disease Ebola virus disease is considered one of the deadliest viral hemorrhagic fevers of the modern era due to its high mortality rate and devastating impact on healthcare systems. The 2014–2016 West African outbreak caused not only severe health consequences but also major economic and social destruction. During the outbreak, infection among healthcare workers highlighted the critical importance of infection prevention and control measures [8]. Ebola outbreaks contributed significantly to strengthening the concept of global health security by promoting the development of early diagnosis systems, contact tracing, isolation practices, field epidemiology, and international coordination mechanisms. Although the development of effective vaccines represents substantial progress, Ebola remains a closely monitored infectious disease due to persistent zoonotic transmission risks and fragile healthcare infrastructures in parts of Africa [8]. 4.4. Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Pandemic COVID-19 became the largest global health crisis of the modern era. The collapse of healthcare systems, shortages in intensive care capacity, disruptions in global supply chains, and vaccine inequities deepened the global consequences of the pandemic. COVID-19 demonstrated that healthcare systems should not be evaluated solely on the basis of hospital capacity. It also revealed the critical importance of data management, digital health technologies, early warning systems, and scientific coordination capacity [9]. 4.5. Mpox (Monkeypox) Mpox is a zoonotic viral infection that has become an important global health concern due to its increasing international spread in recent years. The 2022 global outbreak demonstrated that the disease was not limited to the African continent and could rapidly spread across regions through international travel and close-contact networks. During this period, contact tracing, isolation practices, and community-based awareness campaigns played critical roles in infection control [10]. The mpox outbreak also tested the preparedness of global healthcare systems against emerging infections in the post-COVID-19 era. Although the mortality rate of mpox is lower than that of Ebola or SARS, the disease remains a major public health concern because of its rapid transmission potential and burden on healthcare systems. In particular, insufficient surveillance systems and limited healthcare access in endemic African regions increase the risk of future outbreaks [10]. 4.6. Avian Influenza A/H5N1 (Bird Flu) The H5N1 influenza virus is among the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) viruses and constitutes a major zoonotic threat with global transmission potential through bird populations. Although human infections are relatively rare, the virus causes major public health concerns because of its high mortality rate when transmission occurs. Migratory waterfowl, which serve as the primary reservoirs of the virus, play a critical role in intercontinental spread [11]. In recent years, the ability of H5N1 to infect certain mammalian species in addition to birds has been considered a serious warning regarding the virus’s adaptive capacity. This has raised concerns about the potential emergence of a new Int. J. of Health Serv. Res. and Policy (2026) 11(3):270-280 https://doi.org/10.33457/ijhsrp.1969304 275 influenza pandemic through mutations enabling human-to-human transmission. Consequently, WHO and other international health organizations continue to monitor H5N1 as a virus with high pandemic potential [11]. 4.7. Hantavirus Infection Hantaviruses are zoonotic viruses belonging to the Hantaviridae family. These viruses naturally circulate among rodents and are transmitted to humans through contact with infected rodent urine, feces, or saliva. Transmission generally occurs via aerosolized particles, particularly in rural areas and environments with dense rodent populations. analysis_zh.results: 确定的优势包括医疗基础设施、重症监护能力、数字健康系统和COVID-19经验(A7);挑战涉及人员能力、动物源监测、公共卫生素养、跨部门协作以及对外部生物技术的依赖(A8);气候变化、旅行、迁徙和贸易被视为新发驱动因素(A9);建议的措施包括综合监测、One‐Health协同、国产疫苗/诊断产品生产以及社区教育(A10);分析强调持续的多部门备灾重要性(A11)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究综合现有证据,为国家疫情防备规划提供参考,并强调在土耳其采用One‐Health多部门方法的重要性(A11)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 未在提供的证据中报告

papers.title: Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática
papers.abstract: Objetivo. Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos implicados en el desarrollo del HCPS y su correlación con la severidad de las manifestaciones clínicas de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de la literatura científica sobre la inmunopatogenia de hantavirus sudamericanos bajo los lineamientos PRISMA 2020. Desarrollo. Las variantes de Hantavirus en Bolivia (ANDV, RIOMV y LNV) desencadenan el HCPS. El virus infecta el endotelio sin destruirlo directamente. La variante AND evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral, mientras RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos y perfil Th1/Th17. Esto desregula la permeabilidad capilar, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusiones. El síndrome es una enfermedad inmunomediada donde la severidad depende de la variante genética. El daño tisular no es lítico, sino el resultado de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y una tormenta de citocinas. Comprender esta inmunopatogenia es crucial para diseñar terapias dirigidas a regular la inflamación sistémica.

papers.full_text: 100 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Lilian Verduguez-Orellana1a, Aleida Verduguez-Orellana1,2b Clinical features and immunological events of cardiopulmonary syndrome caused by South American Hantavirus variants: a systematic review Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática DOI: https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 Check for updates En Bolivia circulan las variantes ANDV, RIOMV y LNV, cuya severidad clínica difiere. Objetivo: Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS) y su relación con la gravedad de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos: Revisión sistemática según la declaración PRISMA 2020. Resultados: El virus infecta el endotelio sin daño citopático directo. ANDV evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral; RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos con perfil Th1/Th17; mientras que LNV induce una respuesta equilibrada con oportuna síntesis de interferón tipo I. Estas vías alteran la permeabilidad capilar pulmonar y cardíaca, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusión: El HCPS está mediado por la respuesta inmune y su severidad depende de la variante viral. El daño tisular deriva de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y tormenta de citocinas, por lo que comprender esta inmunopatogenia es esencial para diseñar terapias dirigidas, ya que, no se cuenta con un tratamiento específico. Palabras claves: choque cardiogénico, infecciones por hantavirus, síndrome de dificultad respiratoria del adulto, síndrome pulmonar por hantavirus, tormenta de citocinas. Resumen In Bolivia, the ANDV, RIOMV, and LNV variants circulate, differing in clinical severity. Objective: To analyze the immunopathogenic mechanisms of Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and their relationship with the severity of South American variants. Methods: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: The virus infects the endothelium without direct cytopathic damage. ANDV evades the innate response, accumulating a high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile; whereas LNV induces a balanced response with timely type I interferon synthesis. These pathways alter pulmonary and cardiac capillary permeability, causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock. Conclusion: HCPS is immune-mediated, and its severity depends on the viral variant. Tissue damage stems from an uncontrolled immune response and cytokine storm; thus, understanding this immunopathogenesis is essential to design targeted therapies, as no specific treatment is available. Keywords: cardiogenic shock, hantavirus infections, adult respiratory distress syndrome, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, cytokine storm. Abstract 1Centro Universitario de Medicina Tropical (CUMETROP), Instituto de Investigaciones Biomédicas (IIBISMED), Facultad de Medicina, Universidad Mayor de San Simón, Cochabamba, Bolivia. 2Laboratorio de Radioinmunoensayo, Centro de Medicina Nuclear ahttps://orcid.org/0009-0006-3169-764X lilianverduguez@gmail.com bhttps://orcid.org/0000-0001-7896-9952 a.verduguez@umss.edu *Correspondencia: Aleida Verduguez Orellana Correo electrónico: a.verduguez@umss.edu Recibido el 30 de junio de 2026 Aceptado 16 de septiembre de 2026 https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 L a severidad del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS), desde la perspectiva biológica, es causado por diferentes variantes de hantavirus, que circulan en la región de las américas; siendo la más severa la variante Andes (ANDV)1, 2. En cambio otras variantes tales como Laguna Negra (LNV), Río Mamoré (RIOMV), ocasionan un HCSP entre moderado y leve con mejor pronóstico de recuperación3,4. Desde la perspectiva clínica, el HCPS, como evento, inicia posterior a un período de incubación de unas 2 semanas en promedio4. La fase febril del HCPS inicia con síntomas inespecíficos como fiebre, cefalea, mialgias/artralgias, sintomatología gastrointestinal3,5 y ausencia de sintomatología del tracto respiratorio superior6, estos, aparecerán recién en la fase sindrómica. La fase cardiopulmonar inicia de manera súbita con disnea progresiva acompañada de tos, además de hipoxia severa, la cual se evidencia con cianosis peribucal y desaturación de pulso. Al tercer día el paciente presenta taquicardia e hipotensión3,7. La mitad de los afectados, desarrollan daño renal agudo y un tercio presenta shock. Es en esta fase donde ocurren la gran parte de los decesos3, 6. Los eventos inmunológicos implicados en el desencadenamiento del HCSP independientemente de la variante de hantavirus responsable de la infección, son complejos e interdependientes, con la participación de la inmunidad innata mediante las AR01 Artículos de Revisión Review Article 101 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): células dendríticas y sus productos químicos próximas a las células endoteliales pulmonares, así como también la activación de la inmunidad adaptativa celular, principalmente de linfocitos CD8, complementadas con una desregulación de la respuesta inmune global caracterizada por una tormenta de citocinas4. El objetivo de la presente revisión es analizar los mecanismos inmunológicos que conducen al desarrollo del HCSP por la infección con las variantes de Hantavirus ANDV; RIOMV y LNV que circulan en el territorio boliviano y explicar desde esa perspectiva las manifestaciones clínicas que evidencian la presencia de este síndrome. Metodología Esta revisión sistemática se estructuró siguiendo los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA 2020 y fue registrada en la plataforma internacional PROSPERO con el código CRD420261437203. Consultamos exhaustivamente las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase y Scopus para literatura publicada hasta junio de 2026. Para sistematizar la información, aplicamos una estrategia de búsqueda combinada mediante operadores booleanos (AND, OR) que integró términos MeSH, DeCS y palabras clave en texto libre: ("Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome"[TiAb] OR "Andes virus"[TiAb] OR "Laguna Negra virus"[TiAb] OR "Rio Mamore virus"[TiAb]) AND ("Cytokine Storm"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Innate"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Cellular"[Mesh] OR "Capillary Permeability"[Mesh] OR "immunopathogenesis"[TiAb] OR "immune response"[TiAb] OR "Th1/Th17"[TiAb] OR "VEGF"[TiAb] OR "VE-cadherin"[TiAb]) AND ("South America"[Mesh] OR "Bolivia"[Mesh]). Se incluyo estudios observacionales, ensayos clínicos y modelos experimentales (in vitro e in vivo) enfocados en la inmunopatogenia de estas variantes sudamericanas y su relación con la gravedad clínica. Se excluyeron revisiones puramente narrativas, investigaciones ecológicas o mastozoológicas sin correlación biomédica y trabajos sobre hantavirus del Viejo Mundo. De los 1 585 registros iniciales, eliminamos 435 duplicados y evaluamos 1 150 mediante la lectura de título y resumen. Tras descartar 1 012 artículos irrelevantes, evaluamos el texto completo de 138 contribuciones, excluyendo 109 por deficiencias metodológicas o falta de datos inmunológicos específicos. Finalmente, seleccionamos 28 estudios de alta relevancia para la síntesis cualitativa; el flujo cuantitativo de selección se detalla en el diagrama PRISMA (Figura 1). Tanto el cribado de los registros como la valoración del riesgo de sesgo fueron ejecutados de manera independiente por dos investigadores, detallando la resolución de discrepancias mediante consenso o un tercer revisor. Para la evaluación del riesgo de sesgo, se midió la calidad de los diseños epidemiológicos mediante la Escala Newcastle- AR01 Figura 1. Diagrama de flujo PRISMA del proceso de selección. Elaboración propia. 102 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Ottawa (NOS), incluyendo trabajos con una puntuación ≥ 6 estrellas. En el caso de las investigaciones de ciencia básica, se empleó una lista de parámetros adaptada del Instituto Joanna Briggs (JBI), para constatar el control de variables en los modelos celulares y líneas endoteliales analizadas. Resultados Clínica de la infección por Hantavirus: variantes ANDV, LNV y RIOMV Los hantavirus, variantes RIOMV, LNV, ANDV (circulantes en el territorio boliviano), producen una sintomatología similar entre todos ellos, así como también con otras variantes que circulan en la región de las américas y únicamente se diferencian en cuanto a la severidad del cuadro clínico de la enfermedad que producen1,8. La infección, se inicia por la inhalación de aerosoles procedentes de las excreciones de roedores infectados por partículas virales del grupo de los hantavirus5. Posterior a un período de incubación variable de 9 a 30 días, sin ningún síntoma clínicamente identificable, posteriormente se inicia la fase prodrómica o febril, inespecífica caracterizada por la presencia de fiebre >38 oC, mialgias intensas generalmente en músculos largos, cefalea retroorbitaria y síntomas gastrointestinales como náuseas y/o vómitos y dolor abdominal, el cual suele ser muy intenso, sobre todo cuando la infección es ocasionada por la variante ANDV y puede llegar a confundirse con un cuadro de abdomen agudo y en ciertos casos se puede llegar a evidenciar petequias en región axilar y en extremidades; además son frecuentes las manifestaciones hemorrágicas como la hematuria, metrorragia o hemoptisis2,3,5,9. Durante este período, destaca la ausencia de síntomas del tracto respiratorio superior6. La etapa de transición crítica, comienza al segundo día de iniciada la sintomatología, cuando las variantes implicadas son RIOMV y LNV; en cambio recién inicia al tercer día en el caso de la variante ANDV; esta etapa comprende un período variable AR01 Clínica e inmunología del HCPS Figura 2. Patogénesis comparativa de tres variantes sudamericanas de Hantavirus a nivel del tracto respiratorio. Composición gráfica generada por IA en base a las referencias 1 a 10. Artículos de Revisión Review Article 103 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): de entre 8 a 24 horas6,9, con el comienzo evidente de la fase cardiopulmonar marcada por la aparición súbita de tos seca, disnea, inicialmente leve que progresa rápidamente a grave, y taquipnea (>22 rpm) indicando hipoxia3,8, la misma que, en casos severos, habitualmente relacionados con la infección por la variante ANDV, se manifiesta con cianosis peribucal, además de retracción intercostal y crepitantes bibalares a la auscultación pulmonar7. Al cuarto día, se evidencia taquicardia (>100 lpm) e hipotensión3,5,9. Finalmente, se instaura un edema pulmonar no cardiogénico llevando a una insuficiencia respiratoria aguda y en un 33% de los casos, independientemente de la variante de Hantavirus implicada, se produce shock cardiogénico con resistencia vascular periférica normal con insuficiencia cardíaca congestiva aguda, causando así, la mayor parte de los decesos5,6,9. Los que sobreviven a la fase crítica pasan a la fase de convalecencia que se caracteriza por diuresis elevada, resolución del edema pulmonar en las siguientes 24 a 48 horas y retiro progresivo de la oxigenoterapia. La recuperación completa puede llevar hasta dos años2,5. Existe escasa información clínica específica, respecto a la infección por la variante RIOMV, y se señala que esta variante además de lo señalado anteriormente ocasiona hemorragia intraparenquimal en los dos hemisferios y hemorragia subaracnoidea junto a un cuadro clínico hepatomegalia y daño renal agudo al segundo día7. Por el contrario, en la infección por la variante LNV se evidencia una clínica con menor severidad y mayor incidencia de infecciones leves o subclínicas, con una carga viral baja y una letalidad menor al 20%3,10. Respecto a la variante ANDV, las evidencias clínicas adicionales señalan también la afección del sistema nervioso central con encefalitis acompañada de cefalea intensa y fotofobia11 y una letalidad cercana al 40%2. Infección por Hantavirus variantes sudamericanas y Respuesta inmune Las variantes sudamericanas de hantavirus, infectan las células endoteliales del tracto respiratorio, mediante su acoplamiento a las integrinas αvβ3 y αIIbβ3, alterando el proceso de señalización celular habitual para posibilitar la replicación viral masiva, pero sin ocasionar un efecto citopático directo4,13. La variante ANDV, infecta de la forma anteriormente descrita, vía las integrinas, además de las células epiteliales de los alvéolos respiratorios también a las células de las glándulas salivales humanas1,2,3. Tras su ingreso a la células, la maquinaria viral, mediante su proteína no estructural NSs, inhibe la respuesta inmune innata, por interacción con la proteína adaptadora celular MAVS (Mitochondrial Antiviral-Signaling Protein), bloqueando la producción de los interferones tipo I; al silenciar la producción de estos interferones, la maquinaria viral permite acumular altas cargas virales intracelulares14,15,16, que posteriormente ejercerán un efecto indirecto en el desencadenamiento del HCPS17. Esta evasión inicial de la respuesta inmune innata, además impacta tardíamente en el brazo adaptativo de la respuesta inmune, caracterizado por una desmedida expansión clonal de linfocitos T CD8+ citotóxicos hiperactivados, los cuales migran masivamente al endotelio pulmonar, donde inducen AR01 Figura 3. Fisiopatología del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS). Composición gráfica generada por IA en base a las referencias 4, 24-28. 104 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): AR01 un daño tisular mediado por la acción de perforinas y citocinas proinflamatorias, desestabilizando las uniones intercelulares estrechas sin causar lisis celular directa18. A diferencia de los mecanismos disruptivos de la respuesta inmune empleados por la maquinaria viral de la variante ANDV, la variante RIOMV, una vez ingresada dentro las células endoteliales, promueve la hiperestimulación desregulada de la inmunidad innata a partir de la interacción del RNA viral con los receptores tipo Toll 3 y 7 (TLR-3/7) el RIG-I (Gen I inducible por ácido retinoico), generando una transcripción explosiva de las quimiocinas: RANTES, IP-10 y MCP-1 las cuales a su vez inducen el reclutamiento de monocitos y macrófagos alveolares de forma masiva19. Los monocitos/macrófagos, activan la enzima iNOS y liberan niveles nocivos de óxido nítrico y citocinas pirogénicas (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6)20. A nivel de la respuesta inmune adaptativa, la hiperestimulación desregulada de la respuesta innata, distorsiona el microambiente linfoide, polarizando fuertemente la diferenciación de linfocitos T colaboradores (CD4+) hacia los perfiles efectores Th1 y Th1721. Mientras que la vía Th1 perpetúa el daño celular mediante la liberación sostenida de IFN-γ, el perfil Th17 exacerba el reclutamiento de neutrófilos y desestabiliza directamente la barrera endotelial pulmonar mediante la secreción de IL-1722. Esta sinergia inmunopatológica culmina en una disfunción endotelial profunda, aumento de la permeabilidad capilar y el cuadro grave de SCPH documentado en infecciones por RIOMV3,4,7. El mecanismo empleado por la variante LNV, a diferencia de las dos anteriores, una vez que ingresa a las células endoteliales del tracto respiratorio, es el de estimular un acoplamiento simétrico y controlado entre los componentes innato y adaptativo de la respuesta inmune23. La variante LNV no suprime eficazmente las vías de señalización de los receptores de reconocimiento de patrones (PRRs), permitiendo una síntesis oportuna de IFN Tipo I en las fases iniciales, posibilitando así, la limitación de la replicación microvascular temprana, impidiendo altas cargas virales en el parénquima pulmonar10. A nivel de la respuesta inmune adaptativa, las células dendríticas maduran en un microambiente inflamatorio controlado, favoreciendo una diferenciación linfocitaria T equilibrada eficiente y una rápida maduración de la inmunidad humoral4 (Figura 2). Discusión Síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus y desregulación de la respuesta inmune Clínicamente, el HCPS se origina después de un período variable de incubación viral post infección en función de la variante de Hantavirus implicada2-9; en cambio, los eventos inmunológicos desencadenantes de este síndrome, inician en la etapa temprana de la infección, a partir de la alteración de la integridad de la barrera endotelial, con lo cual se incrementa la permeabilidad vascular, que si bien no es aun clínicamente identificable, la misma, en la etapa sindrómica se verá mucho más incrementada como resultado de la tormenta de citocinas, que se denomina retroalimentación positiva en la afección de la permeabilidad4. La alteración de la integridad de la barrera endotelial, como ya se señaló previamente, responde a la interacción de las variantes de Hantavirus con las moléculas integrinas β3, presentes en las células endoteliales, esta interacción, produce la hipersensibilidad de las células endoteliales el VEGF (Factor de Crecimiento Endotelial Vascular, por sus siglas en inglés) y una inhibición de la capacidad de migración de las células endoteliales sobre vitronectina4,24. El resultado de la acción sinérgica y continua de estos eventos, alteran la capacidad del tejido endotelial de auto reparación y regulación de la permeabilidad capilar y asociado a la inflamación producida por la acción de las quimiocinas y citocinas liberadas por los monocitos/ macrófagos células dendríticas y linfocitos T, provocan una disociación de la VE-cadherina a nivel de las uniones adherentes interendoteliales afectando la función de la barrera endotelial, lo cual permite la formación de espacios intercelulares que permiten el paso masivo de fluido alterando la homeostasis vascular4,19,24. Como parte de la retroalimentación positiva, se activa el sistema calicreína-cinina liberando bradicinina que induce vasodilatación y aumento de la permeabilidad vascular6. full_text_sections.full_text: 100 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): Lilian Verduguez-Orellana1a, Aleida Verduguez-Orellana1,2b Clinical features and immunological events of cardiopulmonary syndrome caused by South American Hantavirus variants: a systematic review Cuadro clínico y eventos inmunológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por variantes Sudamericanas de Hantavirus: revisión sistemática DOI: https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 Check for updates En Bolivia circulan las variantes ANDV, RIOMV y LNV, cuya severidad clínica difiere. Objetivo: Analizar los mecanismos inmunopatológicos del síndrome cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS) y su relación con la gravedad de las variantes sudamericanas. Métodos: Revisión sistemática según la declaración PRISMA 2020. Resultados: El virus infecta el endotelio sin daño citopático directo. ANDV evade la respuesta innata acumulando alta carga viral; RIOMV hiperestimula macrófagos con perfil Th1/Th17; mientras que LNV induce una respuesta equilibrada con oportuna síntesis de interferón tipo I. Estas vías alteran la permeabilidad capilar pulmonar y cardíaca, causando edema pulmonar no cardiogénico y shock cardiogénico. Conclusión: El HCPS está mediado por la respuesta inmune y su severidad depende de la variante viral. El daño tisular deriva de una respuesta inmune descontrolada y tormenta de citocinas, por lo que comprender esta inmunopatogenia es esencial para diseñar terapias dirigidas, ya que, no se cuenta con un tratamiento específico. Palabras claves: choque cardiogénico, infecciones por hantavirus, síndrome de dificultad respiratoria del adulto, síndrome pulmonar por hantavirus, tormenta de citocinas. Resumen In Bolivia, the ANDV, RIOMV, and LNV variants circulate, differing in clinical severity. Objective: To analyze the immunopathogenic mechanisms of Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and their relationship with the severity of South American variants. Methods: Systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: The virus infects the endothelium without direct cytopathic damage. ANDV evades the innate response, accumulating a high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile; whereas LNV induces a balanced response with timely type I interferon synthesis. These pathways alter pulmonary and cardiac capillary permeability, causing non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock. Conclusion: HCPS is immune-mediated, and its severity depends on the viral variant. Tissue damage stems from an uncontrolled immune response and cytokine storm; thus, understanding this immunopathogenesis is essential to design targeted therapies, as no specific treatment is available. Keywords: cardiogenic shock, hantavirus infections, adult respiratory distress syndrome, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, cytokine storm. Abstract 1Centro Universitario de Medicina Tropical (CUMETROP), Instituto de Investigaciones Biomédicas (IIBISMED), Facultad de Medicina, Universidad Mayor de San Simón, Cochabamba, Bolivia. 2Laboratorio de Radioinmunoensayo, Centro de Medicina Nuclear ahttps://orcid.org/0009-0006-3169-764X lilianverduguez@gmail.com bhttps://orcid.org/0000-0001-7896-9952 a.verduguez@umss.edu *Correspondencia: Aleida Verduguez Orellana Correo electrónico: a.verduguez@umss.edu Recibido el 30 de junio de 2026 Aceptado 16 de septiembre de 2026 https://doi.org/10.47993/gmb.v49i2.1344 L a severidad del Síndrome Cardiopulmonar por Hantavirus (HCPS), desde la perspectiva biológica, es causado por diferentes variantes de hantavirus, que circulan en la región de las américas; siendo la más severa la variante Andes (ANDV)1, 2. En cambio otras variantes tales como Laguna Negra (LNV), Río Mamoré (RIOMV), ocasionan un HCSP entre moderado y leve con mejor pronóstico de recuperación3,4. Desde la perspectiva clínica, el HCPS, como evento, inicia posterior a un período de incubación de unas 2 semanas en promedio4. La fase febril del HCPS inicia con síntomas inespecíficos como fiebre, cefalea, mialgias/artralgias, sintomatología gastrointestinal3,5 y ausencia de sintomatología del tracto respiratorio superior6, estos, aparecerán recién en la fase sindrómica. La fase cardiopulmonar inicia de manera súbita con disnea progresiva acompañada de tos, además de hipoxia severa, la cual se evidencia con cianosis peribucal y desaturación de pulso. Al tercer día el paciente presenta taquicardia e hipotensión3,7. La mitad de los afectados, desarrollan daño renal agudo y un tercio presenta shock. Es en esta fase donde ocurren la gran parte de los decesos3, 6. Los eventos inmunológicos implicados en el desencadenamiento del HCSP independientemente de la variante de hantavirus responsable de la infección, son complejos e interdependientes, con la participación de la inmunidad innata mediante las AR01 Artículos de Revisión Review Article 101 G MB julio-diciembre 2026 Gac Med Bol 2026; 49(2): células dendríticas y sus productos químicos próximas a las células endoteliales pulmonares, así como también la activación de la inmunidad adaptativa celular, principalmente de linfocitos CD8, complementadas con una desregulación de la respuesta inmune global caracterizada por una tormenta de citocinas4. El objetivo de la presente revisión es analizar los mecanismos inmunológicos que conducen al desarrollo del HCSP por la infección con las variantes de Hantavirus ANDV; RIOMV y LNV que circulan en el territorio boliviano y explicar desde esa perspectiva las manifestaciones clínicas que evidencian la presencia de este síndrome. Metodología Esta revisión sistemática se estructuró siguiendo los lineamientos de la declaración PRISMA 2020 y fue registrada en la plataforma internacional PROSPERO con el código CRD420261437203. Consultamos exhaustivamente las bases de datos PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase y Scopus para literatura publicada hasta junio de 2026. Para sistematizar la información, aplicamos una estrategia de búsqueda combinada mediante operadores booleanos (AND, OR) que integró términos MeSH, DeCS y palabras clave en texto libre: ("Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus"[Mesh] OR "Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome"[TiAb] OR "Andes virus"[TiAb] OR "Laguna Negra virus"[TiAb] OR "Rio Mamore virus"[TiAb]) AND ("Cytokine Storm"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Innate"[Mesh] OR "Immunity, Cellular"[Mesh] OR "Capillary Permeability"[Mesh] OR "immunopathogenesis"[TiAb] OR "immune response"[TiAb] OR "Th1/Th17"[TiAb] OR "VEGF"[TiAb] OR "VE-cadherin"[TiAb]) AND ("South America"[Mesh] OR "Bolivia"[Mesh]). Se incluyo estudios observacionales, ensayos clínicos y modelos experimentales (in vitro e in vivo) enfocados en la inmunopatogenia de estas variantes sudamericanas y su relación con la gravedad clínica. Se excluyeron revisiones puramente narrativas, investigaciones ecológicas o mastozoológicas sin correlación biomédica y trabajos sobre hantavirus del Viejo Mundo. De los 1 585 registros iniciales, eliminamos 435 duplicados y evaluamos 1 150 mediante la lectura de título y resumen. Tras descartar 1 012 artículos irrelevantes, evaluamos el texto completo de 138 contribuciones, excluyendo 109 por deficiencias metodológicas o falta de datos inmunológicos específicos. Finalmente, seleccionamos 28 estudios de alta relevancia para la síntesis cualitativa; el flujo cuantitativo de selección se detalla en el diagrama PRISMA (Figura 1). Tanto el cribado de los registros como la valoración del riesgo de sesgo fueron ejecutados de manera independiente por dos investigadores, detallando la resolución de discrepancias mediante consenso o un tercer revisor. Para la evaluación del riesgo de sesgo, se midió la calidad de los diseños epidemiológicos mediante la Escala Newcastle- AR01 Figura 1. Diagrama de flujo PRISMA del proceso de selección. analysis.background: The study addresses how South American hantavirus variants (ANDV, RIOMV, LNV) differ in immunopathogenic mechanisms and clinical severity of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS).
analysis.methods: A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines was conducted, examining literature on immunopathogenesis of South American hantavirus variants.
analysis.results: ANDV evades innate immunity, accumulating high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages with a Th1/Th17 profile; LNV elicits a balanced type I interferon response. All variants infect endothelium without direct cytopathic damage, leading to altered capillary permeability, non‑cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and cardiogenic shock. The disease is immune‑mediated, with tissue damage driven by uncontrolled cytokine release.
analysis.contribution: The review clarifies that HCPS severity is variant‑dependent and immune‑mediated, highlighting the need for targeted anti‑inflammatory therapies in the absence of specific antiviral treatment.
analysis.limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The review investigates how South American hantavirus variants (ANDV, RIOMV, LNV) differ in immunopathogenic mechanisms and HCPS severity. Methods: A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines examined literature on immunopathogenesis. Results: ANDV evades innate immunity with high viral load; RIOMV hyperstimulates macrophages (Th1/Th17); LNV induces a balanced type I interferon response. All variants infect endothelium without direct cytopathic damage, causing altered capillary permeability, non‑cardiogenic pulmonary edema, and cardiogenic shock; HCPS is immune‑mediated with cytokine storm–driven tissue damage. Contribution: The study shows HCPS severity depends on viral variant and immune response, underscoring the need for targeted anti‑inflammatory therapies. Limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

papers.title_zh: 南美汉坦病毒变种导致的汉坦病毒心肺综合征的临床表现与免疫事件:系统综述

analysis_zh.background: 本研究探讨南美洲 汉坦病毒 变种(ANDV、RIOMV、LNV)在免疫致病机制和汉坦病毒心肺综合征(HCPS)临床严重程度上的差异。
analysis_zh.methods: 依据 PRISMA 2020 指南,进行系统综述,检索南美洲 汉坦病毒 变种免疫致病机制的文献。
analysis_zh.results: ANDV 逃避先天免疫,导致病毒载量高;RIOMV 过度刺激巨噬细胞,呈 Th1/Th17 型;LNV 引发平衡的 I型干扰素应答。所有变种均感染内皮而不直接导致细胞毒性损伤,进而引起毛细血管通透性改变、非心源性肺水肿和心源性休克。该疾病为免疫介导型,组织损伤由失控的细胞因子释放驱动。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本综述阐明 HCPS 严重程度取决于变种且为免疫介导,强调在缺乏特异性抗病毒治疗的情况下,需要针对性抗炎疗法。
analysis_zh.limitations: 在提供的证据中未报告。

papers.title: Epigenetics of HFRS: Linking Immunity, Pathogenesis, and Vaccine-Induced Protection.
papers.abstract: Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Old World hantaviruses, including Hantaan virus (HTNV) and Seoul virus (SEOV), is an important public-health concern, particularly in Asia. Clinical manifestations range from febrile illness to vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, haemorrhage and acute kidney injury. The mechanisms underlying variation in disease severity and the variability and durability of vaccine-induced immunity remain incompletely understood. papers.title_zh: 肾综合征出血热的表观遗传学:连接免疫、发病机制与疫苗诱导的保护

analysis_zh.background: 肾综合征出血热由旧世界汉坦病毒(HTNV, SEOV)引起,是亚洲重要的公共卫生问题。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述调查了表观遗传对抗病毒免疫的影响,重点关注炎症反应、内皮功能障碍、调控性非编码RNA、训练性免疫以及与疫苗相关的应用。
analysis_zh.current_state: 证据表明表观遗传机制在多种病毒背景下影响免疫,但其在肾综合征出血热(HFRS)严重程度和疫苗诱导保护中的具体作用尚未完全阐明。
analysis_zh.gaps: DNA 甲基化、组蛋白修饰、染色质重塑和 ncRNA 调控对肾综合征出血热结果的直接贡献尚未充分阐明。

papers.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells 1 . However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms-occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus-receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

analysis.background: Hantaviruses are rodent‑borne pathogens that cause severe human disease and lack approved therapeutics (A1).
analysis.methods: The study determined a near‑atomic resolution structure of protocadherin‑1 (PCDH1) bound to the Andes virus spike (A4), performed mutagenesis of Gn loops (A6), and conducted structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies (A7).

analysis.contribution: These findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus‑PCDH1 recognition, reveal a viral strategy of masking the receptor‑binding site, and provide a framework for designing antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike (A8).
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is provided, so detailed experimental procedures, quantitative data, and in‑vivo validation are not reported (abstract_only; A3).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantaviruses cause severe disease and have no approved treatments (A1). Methods: Near‑atomic structural determination of PCDH1‑ANDV spike, Gn loop mutagenesis, and antibody structural/functional analyses were performed (A4, A6, A7). Results: PCDH1 binds a deep pocket formed by four Gn protomers; three Gn loops shape this site and allow cross‑species binding; antibodies block binding by occlusion or steric hindrance (A5, A6, A7). Contribution: The work maps hantavirus‑receptor interactions, explains viral masking of the binding site, and offers a basis for antiviral design (A8). Limitations: Only an abstract is available, lacking detailed methods, quantitative results, and in‑vivo data (abstract_only; A3).

papers.title_zh: 新世界汉坦病毒对前黏附蛋白-1识别的结构基础

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒es 是啮齿动物传播的病原体,导致严重人类疾病,且缺乏获批的治疗方法 (A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究解析了与 安第斯病毒 蛋白棘 (A4) 结合的原粘附蛋白-1 (PCDH1) 的近原子分辨率结构,完成了 Gn 环的定点突变(A6),并对四种中和抗体(A7)进行了结构和功能分析。
analysis_zh.results: PCDH1 与由四个 Gn 蛋白单体形成的深部中心口袋结合,解释了为何需要完整颗粒或可溶性四聚体 (A5);突变分析鉴定出三个塑造受体结合位点并使 PCDH1 结合转移至旧世界糖蛋白的 Gn 环 (A6);抗体通过遮挡该位点或在空间上阻碍结合,从而阻断受体结合 (A7)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 这些发现阐明了 汉坦病毒‐PCDH1 识别的结构决定因素,揭示了病毒掩蔽受体结合位点的策略,并为设计针对 汉坦病毒 蛋白棘的抗病毒治疗剂提供了框架 (A8)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供了摘要,未报告详细的实验步骤、定量数据及体内验证 (abstract_only; A3)。

papers.title: Vascular Programs in Emerging and Re-Emerging RNA Virus Infections: Comparative Lessons from SARS-CoV-2, Flaviviruses, and Hantaviruses.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging RNA viruses frequently present with clinical phenotypes that extend beyond classical organ tropism and include vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation. SARS-CoV-2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses provide three complementary models of virus-induced vascular disease. This narrative review compares these viruses through a shared endothelial-coagulative framework and proposes four partially overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, endothelial barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet quantitative or qualitative dysfunction. These programs are intended as a conceptual synthesis of convergent clinical, pathological, and experimental evidence rather than as a quantitative classification system. The framework is used not only to organize known mechanisms, but also to generate testable predictions for cross-virus biomarker panels, organ-specific endothelial models, and phenotype-guided clinical studies. Severe COVID-19 illustrates inflammation-driven endothelial activation, platelet-leukocyte interactions, complement amplification, NETosis, and immunothrombosis. Within the flavivirus group, DENV is used as the principal model for systemic vascular leakage, thrombocytopenia, and hemorrhagic risk; selected non-dengue flaviviruses illustrate how shared endothelial, platelet, and coagulation modules are redirected toward placental dysfunction (ZIKV), neuroinvasion (WNV and JEV), or hepatic failure and coagulopathy (YFV). Hantavirus infections provide a distinctive model of capillary leak syndrome in which non-lytic endothelial infection, immune-mediated injury, and permeability signaling converge on renal and pulmonary microvascular beds. A comparative view suggests that thrombotic, hemorrhagic, and leaky phenotypes are not mutually exclusive categories, but different outcomes of overlapping vascular programs shaped by viral tropism, vascular-bed specialization, immune activation, and host susceptibility.

analysis.background: Emerging and re‑emerging RNA viruses often cause vascular leakage, platelet dysregulation, coagulation imbalance, microvascular injury, and thromboinflammation, prompting a need to integrate these phenotypes.
analysis.main_directions: The review uses SARS‑CoV‑2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses as complementary models to outline four overlapping vascular programs: endothelial activation, barrier failure, coagulation activation, and platelet dysfunction.
analysis.current_state: A shared endothelial‑coagulative framework synthesizes clinical, pathological and experimental data across the three virus groups, highlighting common mechanisms such as inflammation‑driven endothelial activation and immune‑mediated capillary leak.
analysis.gaps: The proposed programs are conceptual rather than quantitative, indicating limited mechanistic granularity and a need for systematic validation.
analysis.future_research: The authors suggest developing cross‑virus biomarker panels, organ‑specific endothelial models, and phenotype‑guided clinical studies to test the framework.

analysis.summary_en: Background: RNA viruses frequently produce vascular pathology beyond organ tropism. Main directions: SARS‑CoV‑2, flaviviruses, and hantaviruses illustrate four overlapping vascular programs. Current state: A shared endothelial‑coagulative framework integrates clinical and experimental evidence of endothelial activation, barrier failure, coagulation, and platelet dysfunction. Gaps: The framework remains conceptual, lacking quantitative classification and systematic validation. Future research: Build cross‑virus biomarker panels, organ‑specific endothelial models, and phenotype‑guided clinical trials.

papers.title_zh: 新发和再新发RNA病毒感染中的血管程序:来自SARS-CoV-2、黄病毒和汉坦病毒的比较经验。

analysis_zh.background: 新发和再发RNA病毒常导致血管渗漏、血小板功能失调、凝血失衡、微血管损伤以及血栓炎症,因而需要将这些表型进行整合。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒以及汉坦病毒es为互补模型,概述四个相互重叠的血管程序:内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍。
analysis_zh.current_state: 一个共享的内皮‐凝血框架整合了三类病毒的临床、病理和实验数据,突出共同机制,如炎症驱动的内皮激活和免疫介导的毛细血管渗漏。
analysis_zh.gaps: 所提出的程序是概念性的而非定量的,表明机制细节有限且需要系统性验证。
analysis_zh.future_research: 作者建议开发跨病毒生物标志物面板、器官特异性内皮模型以及基于表型的临床研究,以检验该框架。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：新发和再发RNA病毒常导致血管渗漏、血小板功能失调、凝血失衡、微血管损伤以及血栓炎症,因而需要将这些表型进行整合。 主要方向：本综述以SARS‐CoV‐2、黄病毒以及汉坦病毒es为互补模型,概述四个相互重叠的血管程序:内皮激活、屏障失效、凝血激活和血小板功能障碍。 研究现状：一个共享的内皮‐凝血框架整合了三类病毒的临床、病理和实验数据,突出共同机制,如炎症驱动的内皮激活和免疫介导的毛细血管渗漏。 不足：所提出的程序是概念性的而非定量的,表明机制细节有限且需要系统性验证。 后续研究：作者建议开发跨病毒生物标志物面板、器官特异性内皮模型以及基于表型的临床研究,以检验该框架。

papers.title: Can Hantavirus cruise into the next pandemic?
papers.abstract: Despite concerns arising from a recent ship-associated outbreak on the M/V Hondius cruise, current evidence suggests that Andes virus (ANDV) poses a low pandemic risk. Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.

Nevertheless, viral evolution, ecological changes, and reservoir host dynamics could drive future emergence of ANDV, underscoring the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccine preparedness.

papers.title: Vaccines Against Hantavirus Infections: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hantaviruses infections are responsible for a hemorrhagic fever with renal and cardiopulmonary syndrome with case-fatality rates up to 50%. While inactivated vaccines are already available in China and South Korea, several additional candidate vaccines are under development. This systematic review summarizes the current clinical evidence on immunogenicity and short-term safety of vaccines targeting different hantavirus strains. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic literature search was carried out to identify randomized and nonrandomized trials of any phase. Data were synthesized narratively within strata defined by vaccine platform, target virus, assay, immunogenicity and safety. Results: Ten trials on 961 adults were included: four single-arm trials on the inactivated vaccine and six early-phase DNA-vaccine trials. One month after last dose, the inactivated vaccine achieved neutralizing seropositivity by PRNT 50 in 45.1% of the tested subjects after two priming doses and 55.7% after three, while the corresponding binding-antibody values measured by IFA were 87.3% and 95.7%. Among DNA vaccines, homologous responses reached 100% against HTNV and 83.3% against PUUV with monovalent constructs, whereas dual responses to the bivalent construct were registered in 33.3% and 77.8% of the subjects, when measured through PRNT 50 and PsVNA 50 , respectively. One serious adverse event occurred, most likely unrelated to vaccination. Conclusions: No serious safety signal was identified, although safety remains insufficiently characterized. Measured immunogenicity depends as much on the assay as on the vaccine, and, in the absence of a validated correlate of protection, it cannot be read as a clinical benefit. Future research should prioritize validated correlates of protection and innovative trial designs adapted to low-incidence diseases.

analysis.background: Hantavirus infections cause hemorrhagic fever with renal and cardiopulmonary syndrome and can have case‑fatality rates up to 50%, prompting vaccine development.
analysis.main_directions: The review covers licensed inactivated vaccines in China/South Korea and multiple early‑phase DNA vaccine candidates, evaluating immunogenicity across different hantavirus strains and assay platforms.
analysis.current_state: Ten trials (961 adults) show modest neutralizing seropositivity for inactivated vaccines (45‑56%) and higher binding‑antibody rates, while DNA vaccines achieve up to 100% homologous responses; safety signals are minimal but not fully characterized, and no validated correlate of protection exists.
analysis.gaps: Safety data remain limited, immunogenicity results vary by assay, and the absence of a protective correlate hampers efficacy interpretation.
analysis.future_research: Prioritize establishing validated correlates of protection and designing innovative trials suited to the low‑incidence nature of hantavirus disease.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hantavirus infections cause severe hemorrhagic fever with high fatality, driving vaccine research. Main directions: Review examines licensed inactivated vaccines and early DNA vaccine candidates across strains and assays. Current state: Ten trials show modest neutralizing responses for inactivated vaccines, higher for DNA vaccines, with minimal serious safety events but no protective correlate. Gaps: Safety characterization is incomplete, assay‑dependent immunogenicity limits conclusions, and lack of a correlate of protection persists. Future research: Develop validated correlates and innovative trial designs for this low‑incidence disease.

papers.title_zh: 针对汉坦病毒感染的疫苗:系统文献综述。

analysis_zh.background: 汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,病例致死率最高可达50%,促使疫苗研发。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述涵盖中国/韩国已获许可的灭活疫苗以及多种早期DNA疫苗候选,评估不同汉坦病毒毒株和检测平台的免疫原性。
analysis_zh.current_state: 十项试验(961名成人)显示灭活疫苗的中和抗体阳性率适中(45‐56%),结合抗体率更高;DNA疫苗可达100%同源应答;安全信号极少但尚未完全表征,且缺乏经验证的保护相关指标。
analysis_zh.gaps: 安全性数据仍有限,免疫原性结果随检测方法而异,缺乏保护相关指标阻碍疗效解读。
analysis_zh.future_research: 应优先建立经验证的保护相关指标,并设计适合汉坦病毒低发病率特征的创新性试验。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：汉坦病毒感染导致肾综合征出血热和汉坦病毒心肺综合征,病例致死率最高可达50%,促使疫苗研发。 主要方向：本综述涵盖中国/韩国已获许可的灭活疫苗以及多种早期DNA疫苗候选,评估不同汉坦病毒毒株和检测平台的免疫原性。 研究现状：十项试验(961名成人)显示灭活疫苗的中和抗体阳性率适中(45‐56%),结合抗体率更高;DNA疫苗可达100%同源应答;安全信号极少但尚未完… 不足：安全性数据仍有限,免疫原性结果随检测方法而异,缺乏保护相关指标阻碍疗效解读。 后续研究：应优先建立经验证的保护相关指标,并设计适合汉坦病毒低发病率特征的创新性试验。

papers.title: Host-Virus Immune Interactions in Andes Virus Infection: Implications for Human-to-Human Transmission, Pathogenesis, and Public Health.
papers.abstract: The Andes virus (ANDV, Orthohantavirus , andesense) is unique among hantaviruses in that it may transfer from person to person and cause severe vascular damage. The evidence on host-virus immunological interactions and their importance in disease progression, transmission, and public health is compiled in this narrative review. ANDV mostly affects pulmonary endothelial cells and does not result in widespread cell loss. Rather, the loss of vascular barrier integrity is caused by vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling, Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) activation, breakdown of vascular endothelial (VE)-cadherin, hypoxia-related pathways, and mediators produced from infected pericytes. Additionally, the virus interferes with early antiviral defenses involving protein kinase R (PKR), TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1)-interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS), and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5). analysis.background: Andes virus (ANDV) is the only hantavirus known to transmit between humans and cause severe vascular injury.
analysis.main_directions: The review synthesizes current knowledge on host‑virus immune interactions, focusing on endothelial pathology, innate antiviral evasion, cytokine responses, and implications for transmission and public health.
analysis.current_state: ANDV primarily targets pulmonary endothelial cells, leading to loss of vascular barrier integrity via VEGF signaling, RhoA activation, VE‑cadherin disruption, hypoxia pathways, and pericyte‑derived mediators.
analysis.gaps: Detection of viral RNA in blood and secretions does not confirm infectious virus, limiting understanding of the true infectious period.
analysis.future_research: Prospective studies integrating serial virological sampling, genomic sequencing, and standardized exposure assessment are needed to delineate the infectious phase and transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Andes virus (ANDV) is the only hantavirus known to transmit between humans and cause severe vascular injury. Main directions: The review synthesizes current knowledge on host‑virus immune interactions, focusing on endothelial pathology, innate antiviral evasion, cytokine responses, and implications for transmission and public health. Current state: ANDV primarily targets pulmonary endothelial cells, leading to loss of vascular barrier integrity via VEGF signaling, RhoA activation, VE‑cadherin disruption, hypoxia pathways, and pericyte‑derived mediators. Gaps: Detection of viral RNA in blood and secretions does not confirm infectious virus, limiting understanding of the true infectious period. Future research: Prospective studies integrating serial virological sampling, genomic sequencing, and standardized exposure assessment are needed to delineate the infectious phase and transmission dynamics.

papers.title_zh: 安第斯病毒 感染中的宿主-病毒免疫相互作用:对人际传播、发病机制及公共卫生的意义。

analysis_zh.background: 安第斯病毒(ANDV)是唯一已知能够在人与人之间传播并导致严重血管损伤的汉坦病毒。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述综合了当前关于宿主‐病毒免疫相互作用的认识,重点关注内皮病理、先天抗病毒逃逸、细胞因子反应及其对传播和公共卫生的意义。
analysis_zh.current_state: ANDV 主要攻击肺部内皮细胞,通过 VEGF 信号、RhoA 激活、VE‐钙黏蛋白破坏、缺氧通路以及周细胞来源的介质导致血管屏障完整性丧失。
analysis_zh.gaps: 在血液和分泌物中检测到病毒 RNA 并不等同于存在传染性病毒,这限制了对真实传染期的认识。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要前瞻性研究将连续病毒学采样、基因组测序和标准化暴露评估相结合,以阐明传染阶段和传播动态。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：安第斯病毒(ANDV)是唯一已知能够在人与人之间传播并导致严重血管损伤的汉坦病毒。 主要方向：本综述综合了当前关于宿主‐病毒免疫相互作用的认识,重点关注内皮病理、先天抗病毒逃逸、细胞因子反应及其对传播和公共卫生的意义。 研究现状：ANDV 主要攻击肺部内皮细胞,通过 VEGF 信号、RhoA 激活、VE‐钙黏蛋白破坏、缺氧通路以及周细胞来源的介质导致血管屏障完整性丧失。 不足：在血液和分泌物中检测到病毒 RNA 并不等同于存在传染性病毒,这限制了对真实传染期的认识。 后续研究：需要前瞻性研究将连续病毒学采样、基因组测序和标准化暴露评估相结合,以阐明传染阶段和传播动态。
